ca_lower_cliffs_lower_tier.blurb: A short face crag in the Indian Springs area along the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe, sitting at roughly 5,700 feet. Walls top out around 50 feet, with thirteen routes mixing bolted leads, a few trad lines and a single top rope. Most climbs fall in the 5.9 range, with a few easier ones in the 5.6 to 5.8 band and a couple of 5.10s, so it suits climbers learning to read granite face holds. The rock is solid and featured, and the bolts can sit well apart in places, so a small rack is worth carrying on the sparser leads. Every route has anchors. It is the first wall you meet on the walk in.

ca_great_stone_face.blurb: A small boulder cluster inside a neighborhood rock park in Berkeley's Northbrae district, in the East Bay. Thirteen problems are on record here, running from an easy slab through the middle grades up to a few very hard lines, with the namesake face being the headline problem. The rock is the hard volcanic rhyolite typical of the Berkeley hills, with a grassy lawn and trees around the stones. It sees little traffic compared with the bigger Berkeley rock parks, making it a quiet stop for a short session. Street parking is available nearby, and a crash pad is the only real gear needed.

ca_dude_ranch_the.blurb: A sport crag tucked away in Box Canyon West, in the high desert near Barstow, at roughly 3,800 feet. Thirteen climbs, nearly all bolted, cluster around the 5.10 and 5.11 range with one easier line and a pair of 5.12s, plus a lone trad route. The rock runs from plumb to a touch past vertical; the hard moves come early and low, then ease off higher up. It is out of sight yet close to the road, and the quiet desert setting means few other parties. Pick a warmer day to take advantage of the shade the face holds for most of the day.

ca_central_cottage_dome.blurb: The middle of the three Cottage Domes near Tuolumne Meadows in Yosemite, at roughly 8,950 feet. It is a long curving face with plenty of face climbing and several cracks. Thirteen routes are on record, ranging from 5.9 up to 5.12, with most of them in the 5.11 and 5.12 grades, so this is more a stop for experienced climbers than for beginners. Lines include trad, bolted and top-rope options. The dome is a short walk north of West Cottage Dome, which makes it easy to pair with its neighbors, and it sees fewer parties than the popular east dome.
ca_central_cottage_dome.approach: From West Cottage Dome, walk north for about five minutes.

ca_meilee_area.blurb: A sector of the Lizard's Mouth sandstone boulders in the mountains above Santa Barbara, at roughly 3,000 feet. Thirteen problems run from easy warm-ups at V0 through a good middle band of V2 to V4 to a few harder lines in the V6 and V7 range. The headline is the Meilee traverse in the cave, with several popular exit problems nearby, plus a slab and some crack and finger-crack lines. The Lizard's Mouth is a compact area rather than a big one, so it works well as a short session. Bring a pad.

ca_jacked_and_tan.blurb: A single huge boulder at Potter's Point, near the top of Gibraltar Road above Santa Barbara, that carries all thirteen problems here. Expect many traverses and sit starts, with grades spread from V1 through the middle range to a few at V8 and V9, and a good number of problems in the V3 to V7 zone. It is a compact stop within a bigger area of mostly scattered boulders, where the rock is coarse and can be rough on skin. It is reached by a trail of about fifteen minutes from the road, and a pad and spotter are standard.

ca_moon_the_2.blurb: The biggest and steepest dome at Moonlight Crags in the Lost Sierra of northeastern California, rising about 200 feet at an elevation of roughly 5,250 feet. The rhyolite is rough and featured, with excellent friction. Most of the thirteen routes are set up as top ropes, with a couple of trad lines, and the grades are friendlier than the steepness suggests, from 5.6 up to a handful of 5.10s and one or two 5.11 and 5.12 routes. It faces east, so it gets morning sun. The walk in is a flat stroll of about half a mile or a little more, and reaching the top involves some exposed scrambling or rappels.

ca_amphitheater_the_2.blurb: A compact boulder in the Moby Dick section of Santee Boulders, in San Diego County, just left of the big Moby Dick boulder itself. It has a concave wall facing south, which means it takes plenty of sun. Thirteen problems run mostly V0 to V4, with traverses and incline lines for easy volume, and a handful of harder ones reaching V7 on the sit starts. It is a good stop for beginners and a casual circuit, with approach directions shared with the rest of the Moby Dick area. A crash pad is the main thing to pack.
